name: Ninja
listed_description: Build system the book uses with CMake to compile LLVM, chosen because it is fast and available on all platforms.
listed_license: Apache-2.0 (from the repository page, not stated in the book)
claim_text: Ninja is used because it is fast and available on all platforms; by default it uses all CPU cores.
book_benchmark: None. Qualitative statement only; no timings, baseline or hardware given for the comparison.
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 1, Getting the prerequisites ready

name: Hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser (tinylang)
listed_description: Book builds a lexer and a recursive-descent parser by hand, using a keyword hash table (llvm::StringMap) and zero-terminated MemoryBuffer input so no length check is needed per character; says compilers favor this for compile speed.
claim_text: As compilation speed matters, many compilers use a handwritten lexer, with one example being clang.
book_benchmark: None. Book gives no timings; generated state-machine parsers are described as possibly slower than recursive descent, without measurement.
guessed_baseline: flex and bison generated lexer and parser
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 2, A hand-written lexer; ch. 3, Structuring the lexer and Constructing a recursive descent parser (closing discussion of parser generators)

name: Perfect-hash interface vtable lookup
listed_description: Idea of replacing a linear search through interface vtables with a compile-time perfect hash from interface id (for example an MD5 of the symbol) to vtable, giving constant-time interface method dispatch.
claim_text: The result is much faster than the linear search and only takes constant time.
book_benchmark: None. Design discussion only; no code in the companion repository and no measurements.
guessed_baseline: linear search through the list of interface vtables
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 5, Extending single inheritance with interfaces

name: Depth-first numbering for constant-time class hierarchy type test
listed_description: Number classes of a known hierarchy in depth-first order so a runtime type test becomes a compare against a number or interval; the book says LLVM's own RTTI works this way.
claim_text: The type test becomes compare-against-a-number or an interval, which can be done in constant time.
book_benchmark: None. Contrasted qualitatively with walking the inheritance chain up to the root class; no timings.
guessed_baseline: vtable-pointer comparison walking up the base class chain (dynamic_cast-style test)
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 5, Implementing single inheritance

name: Braun et al. SSA construction with phi simplification
listed_description: The book's code generator builds SSA form directly from the AST with the Simple and Efficient Construction algorithm (Braun et al., CC 2013), plus removal of trivial phi nodes, instead of emitting alloca/load/store and relying on mem2reg.
claim_text: Even without this optimization, this algorithm runs very fast.
book_benchmark: None. The book notes the load-and-store approach produces many instructions LLVM later removes; no timings of either approach.
guessed_baseline: alloca/load/store code generation followed by the mem2reg pass
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 4, Generating IR from the AST, sections Learning about the load-and-store approach and Optimizing the generated phi instructions

name: LLVM_OPTIMIZED_TABLEGEN build option
listed_description: CMake option that builds the tablegen tool with optimization even in a debug LLVM build, to cut compile time of generated code-generator sources.
claim_text: tablegen is much slower in a debug build, increasing the compile time noticeably; this option may reduce compile time.
book_benchmark: None. No timings given; default is OFF.
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 1, Customizing the build process, Table 1.3

name: LLVM_USE_SPLIT_DWARF build option
listed_description: CMake option that has gcc or clang write DWARF debug information into separate files, shrinking object files so debug builds link faster.
claim_text: The reduced size of the object files reduces the link time of debug builds significantly.
book_benchmark: None. No timings, baseline or hardware given; default is OFF.
guessed_baseline: debug build with DWARF embedded in object files
found_in: book: Learn LLVM 17, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 1, Customizing the build process, Table 1.3
